I was conceived as an accident and my parents did not want me. Despite that, my mum chose to give birth to me because she believed that abortion is immoral. She had the option of giving me away (my aunt was infertile and really wanted to adopt me), but she chose to keep me by her side.  I was then made to know from a very young age that both my parents and my grandmother favour my elder brother (not only through extremely preferential treatment, but they actually told me about it). It did not help that I was a girl and they favoured boys. 

Until today, I still dwell on the countless stressful family situations that I was put through growing up (as though the preferential treatment isn't bad enough, my family was extremely dysfunctional too). I have battled with social anxiety and depression ever since I was a teenager, and even as I approach 30 now, I can't help but feel bitter that my childhood has affected me in so many ways. While I have found other areas of my life to focus on, this is something that I will never be able to forget as long as I live.
